newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia says suspends new dealings with Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia says suspends new dealings with Singapore.

text.p: Malaysia said on Wednesday it was suspending new bilateral dealings with Singapore, the national news agency Bernama said.
The decision was made at the weekly cabinet meeting chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, Bernama said, quoting several cabinet ministers whom it did not name.
At last week's cabinet meeting, the government announced that it had accepted an apology by Singapore Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew for making disparaging remarks about crime in a Malaysian state.
But Foreign Minister Abdullah Ahmad Badawi said last week that the episode had deeply offended Malaysians and "restoration of the old level of relationship would take time".
Lee also said last week that he had instructed his lawyer to delete remarks made in a court affidavit that the neighbouring state of Johor was "notorious for shootings, muggings and car-jackings".
